newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends down on RBI, state dollar buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends down on RBI, state dollar buying.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended at 35.87/88 against the dollar on Tuesday, down from the opening quote of 35.86/87, dealers said.
They said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) bought dollars at noon and in the evening at 35.87 a dollar -- the highest price it has been paying for dollars in recent months.
Dealers said the RBI was gently nudging the rupee down without inviting undue attention. It was buying dollars after about a week. Its last purchase price was 35.85, they said.
Many dealers said the rupee was overvalued especially after the dollar's recent gains against major global currencies.
A leading Calcutta-based state-run bank bought dollars towards the close of the session on Tuesday, helping the dollar to end up, dealers said.
Forward dollar premia edged up largely because of banks seeking to book forward dollars against payment of premia.
This was in a large measure induced by the rising trend in overnight call money rates which closed at 5.5 percent on Tuesday, up from 1.0-2.0 percent level last week, dealers said.
